carousel.cover_headline:
Eating Ultra-Processed Food Daily
May Be Linked to Early
Parkinson's Signs

slides.label: THE STUDY
slides.headline: 42,853 people tracked for up to 26 years
slides.insight: Researchers tracked diet and early Parkinson's signs over decades.

slides.label: THE FINDING
slides.headline: High intake group had **2.5 times** the risk of early Parkinson's signs
slides.insight: "High" meant 11 or more servings of ultra-processed food per day.
slides.image_prompt: potato chips soda cans packaged snacks

slides.label: EVEN A LITTLE
slides.headline: Even low intake: packaged candy linked to 60% higher risk
slides.insight: Sauces and condiments were linked to 17% higher risk in the low-intake group.

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
slides.headline: Additives may promote oxidative stress in the brain
slides.insight: Free radicals may damage dopamine-producing neurons, researchers suggest.
slides.image_prompt: fresh whole foods wet market vegetables

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Swap one packaged snack for a whole food instead
slides.insight: Fresh fruit, boiled egg, or plain nuts — real food, fewer additives.

sources: Neurology (journal), study reported by The Standard (HK), 2026
carousel.caption:
Eating ultra-processed food daily may be linked to early Parkinson's signs.

A study in Neurology followed 42,853 people for up to 26 years. Those eating 11 or more servings of ultra-processed food daily were associated with 2.5 times the risk of early Parkinson's signs compared to low-intake groups. Even small amounts of packaged candy were linked to 60% higher risk in the low-intake group.

What is one packaged food your family reaches for most often?

Not medical advice.

Sources: Neurology journal, 2026 (reported by The Standard HK)
